principle: Every visible MMIR control must either perform a useful action, be disabled with a clear reason, or be truthfully labeled beta/planned/premium.
public_repo_rule: This manifest is public-safe. It documents UI behavior only; no secrets, provider keys, billing policy or private user data belong here.

groups.user_result: A new visitor can type or choose a starter prompt and get a useful free browser answer before setup.
The public homepage keeps local-only usage analytics controllable by the user without cookies or external tracking.
The + Connect Model control creates or reuses the free local-node profile, makes it active and opens the setup panel.
The automatic launch checklist shows Browser ready, Private mode, Local node, Model live and First chat gates without asking the user to configure first.
Users can save, activate, open and delete backend profiles without placing provider keys in the public frontend.
Users can refresh models, stop a running response, clear local chat history, copy/retry answers and switch functional modes.
Users can refresh local-node status, open settings and request/stop a free tunnel through paired local-node routes; unsupported tunnel control returns a clear safe error.
Users can see active node health, hardware, models, tunnel state, cross-device pairing code and exact next repair action from one local-first dashboard.
Live backend models are preferred automatically; browser helpers, WebGPU models and installable free Ollama models remain visible with license/source guidance.
evidence: Source/model card: verify before production use

groups.user_result: Users can choose an installable-free Ollama model, start a paired local-node install job, watch pull progress and refresh into a live model.
The owner can refresh public-safe platform status, backlog progress, GUI parity and user journey state from the site.

groups.surface: Workspace, memory, knowledge and privacy controls
groups.user_result: Users can create local workspaces, store memory/knowledge, stage files with previews, sync when a protected backend exists, and export/delete local data.
Users can save, rename, pin, archive, search, load, fork, export and safe-share local conversations per workspace.
Users can define workflows, datasets and planning-only training jobs through protected backend contracts without starting paid compute.
Paid/provider-backed routes stay visible as future capability but blocked behind protected backend routing, auth, rate limits, audit and cost policy.
evidence: Provider keys must stay behind a protected backend
